title: Polish Armed Forces
capsule: Following the November 11, 1918 armistice and Poland's proclamation of independence under Józef Piłsudski, the Polish Armed Forces were constituted from three different military traditions: the Polish Legions trained in Austria-Hungary, Józef Haller's Blue Army formed in France, and units emerging from the dissolved Russian imperial forces. During the attested window (1918–1919) these forces simultaneously fought to secure Poland's borders in the Polish-Ukrainian War over eastern Galicia (1918–1919), the Greater Poland Uprising against Germany (December 1918), and preliminary clashes that prefigured the Polish-Soviet War. The reconstituted armed forces defined Poland's territorial shape through combat rather than diplomacy in nearly all directions during this founding period.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. This entry represents a transitional military-political entity rather than a stable polity; territorial extent during 1918–1919 was rapidly changing and contested on multiple fronts, making precise boundary attestation inherently limited.
